effects: Pulls `assets` ftUSD (ASSET, 0xF7D8…9C9C) from the signer into the vault (safeTransferFrom in _deposit).
Mints the same number of sftUSD shares (1:1) to `receiver`, which then earns FT rewards by stake-time.
The vault moves the ftUSD into the yield wrapper (yieldWrapper.deposit). This is the vault's own asset; the signer's balances do not change from it.
Checkpoints reward accrual for `receiver` (_settleUser / _accrueOpenStakeTime). Nothing is paid out.
formats.shown: "Stake <amount> ftUSD", with the amount and the receiver of the stake as fields.

findings.title: deposit: interpolatedIntent leaves out the receiver, who gets the sftUSD stake position.
findings.evidence: EpochRewardsVault.sol deposit → _deposit(msg.sender, receiver, …) → _mint(to, shares). descriptor interpolatedIntent "Stake {assets}". Receiver is only a separate field.

findings.title: deposit: the ftUSD token constant is the mainnet address but is also used for the Sonic (146) deployment.
findings.evidence: descriptor params.token 0xF7D85EC4E7710f71992752eac2111312e73E9C9C is the same for deployments 1 and 146. Mainnet impl meta immutables show ASSET = 0xf7d85ec4…. No chain-146 source is here to confirm that ftUSD has the same address there.
findings.fix: Confirm that ftUSD on chain 146 is at 0xF7D8…9C9C. If it is not, split the descriptor per chain with the correct token address.

findings.title: deposit: test amount is 1e18 for a 6-decimal token, so the screen shows 1,000,000,000,000 ftUSD.
findings.evidence: cases/0.json data assets=0x0de0b6b3a7640000, screen "1000000000000 ftUSD". EpochRewardsVault.sol decimals comment: ftUSD uses 6 decimals.
findings.fix: Use a realistic 6-decimal amount, such as 1000000 for 1 ftUSD.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner)
effects: Burns `assets` sftUSD shares (1:1) from `owner`. If owner is not the signer, it spends owner's sftUSD allowance to the signer.
Calls yieldWrapper.withdraw(assets, receiver): ftUSD goes to `receiver`, either now or through a withdrawal queue entry (a queueId is returned).
Settles `owner`'s FT reward accrual up to now. Accrued FT stays claimable and is not paid.
formats.shown: "Unstake <amount> ftUSD", with the amount, the receiver and the owner as fields.

findings.title: withdraw: the payout can be queued in the yield wrapper, but "Unstake" suggests ftUSD arrives now.
findings.evidence: EpochRewardsVault.sol _withdrawWithQueueIds: queueIdTo = yieldWrapper.withdraw(assets, receiver). withdrawWithQueueId doc: "return the yield wrapper queue ID (0 when immediate)". The descriptor intent is "Unstake ftUSD".
findings.fix: If the wrapper can queue, say so in the intent or add a notice, such as "Unstake ftUSD (may be queued)".

findings.title: withdraw: interpolatedIntent leaves out the receiver of the ftUSD.
withdraw: the ftUSD token constant is hardcoded from mainnet and reused for the chain 146 deployment.
findings.evidence: descriptor params.token 0xF7D85EC4… is used for deployments 1 and 146. It cannot be confirmed for 146 from the sources here.
findings.fix: Confirm the address per chain, or split the descriptor per chain.

effects: Settles the signer's FT reward accrual for epochs that are already settled.
Sends min(accrued FT, the vault's FT balance) to `to`. The amount comes from storage, not calldata.
Any part it cannot pay stays recorded as accrued for the signer.
formats.shown: "Claim FT to <to>", with the recipient as a field.

findings.title: claim: the FT amount paid comes from storage and is capped by the vault's balance, so it cannot be shown.
findings.evidence: EpochRewardsVault.sol _claim: claimable = user.ftAccrued; paidGross = claimable <= bal ? claimable : bal; FT.safeTransfer(to, paidToUser).
findings.fix: None possible in the descriptor. The intent could say "Claim all settled FT rewards".

couldNotCheck: The yield wrapper at 0xB44a9C40EFc05Eb014EfFEac3CBed6A31F8cB87f (constructor arg _yieldWrapper) is not in the directory. It runs yieldWrapper.withdraw(assets, receiver) in withdraw, which decides whether, when and how much ftUSD the receiver gets, or whether the withdrawal is queued.
